title: Budget 2026: Breathing space for today, hope for the future
text:
• Chancellor John Healey delivers a Budget to give families and businesses breathing space from rising costs, with action on energy bills, fuel duty, wages and the everyday cost of living. 

 • Investment to get Britain building and growing, backing homes, high streets and British businesses while strengthening energy and national security. 

 • Fair choices maintain economic stability, with the Government cutting borrowing and meeting its fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.

 The Chancellor has unveiled a Budget that gives families and businesses breathing space today, while delivering the big structural changes needed for the future.  

 Against a backdrop of global uncertainty and pressure on household budgets, the Budget takes action on energy and motoring costs, backs wages and high streets, helps more people onto the housing ladder, and supports British businesses to invest and grow – while strengthening Britain’s national security. 

 Built on fiscal discipline, the Budget will provide the bedrock for our economy to continue to grow and deliver the vision that the Prime Minster will set out in his 10-year plan.

 Breathing Space 

 Families and businesses will get breathing space from rising costs, with major action on energy, driving and everyday bills alongside support for wages, housing and high streets. Alongside immediate support, the Budget fundamentally sets a new pathway for the energy system to deliver cheaper, more secure energy in the long-term. 

 Households: 

 • 
 Lower energy bills: In 2027 the government is providing a £100 Household Energy Payment for up to 20 million households in bands A to D in England, with funding for similar support provided to the rest of the UK, while the temporary VAT cut on electricity bills will be extended until 1 July 2027, taking around £50 off the Ofgem annual price cap in April 2027. This will be paid for by increasing the Bank Corporation Tax Surcharge from 3% to 6% for 15 months, before ending on 31 March 2028. 

 • 
 Long-term energy reform: From 2027 the government will introduce a new comprehensive framework at the spending review that ensures government action drives costs down over the next ten years. Until that framework is in place, no further policy costs will be placed on bills unless they bring bills down or are essential to keep the lights on. We will take that approach in our next renewables auction, Allocation Round 8, to ensure that we only buy cheap clean power that is ready to connect to the grid. The tax on gas bills planned by the previous government to fund hydrogen will be scrapped and planned hydrogen projects will instead be publicly funded. 

 • 
 Standing charges: The government will also ask Ofgem to abolish gas standing charges and move them to unit rates, making bills fairer and giving households more control over what they pay. Households not seeing an automatic saving will still have better control over their bills without the worry of affording the standing charge, and the government will set out targeted mitigation in due course. 

 • 
 Making energy cheaper and more secure: In 2028-30, the government will reduce Britain’s exposure to volatile international gas prices, ensuring new clean power delivers value for billpayers and delivers cheaper and faster grid connections.  

 • 
 Paternity: The government is extending parental pay to more than 160,000 additional parents, including self-employed dads and partners who have previously missed out. 

 • 
 Making everyday life easier: 1,000 Post Office parcel drop boxes will be rolled out and 600 branches upgraded by the end of the financial year, while the new Warm Homes loans scheme will help households spread the upfront cost of solar panels, batteries and heat pumps, which together could cut bills by up to £550 a year. 

 • 
 Higher wages: On 1 April 2027, the National Living Wage will increase by 3.9% to £13.21 per hour. This uplift represents an increase of £910 to the gross annual earnings of a full-time worker on the National Living Wage. 

 • 
 Everyday costs: Tariffs will be removed from more than 100 products, helping lower import costs on family favourites including baked beans and chocolate, alongside tariff cuts on kerosene and fertiliser to support households and farmers facing higher costs.

 Support for drivers 

 This Budget also supports drivers by extending the 5p cut to fuel duty for a further six months, and deferring the planned Retail Prices Index (RPI) increase, to 1 July 2027, to support households and businesses. 

 • 
 Saving money: Taken together, the government’s decisions on fuel duty across this Parliament will save the average car driver £230, the average large goods driver saves £472 and the average heavy goods driver nearly £4000 compared to plans under the previous government, and means petrol and diesel will be 15p per litre cheaper from April 2027.  

 • 
 Backing people who drive for work: To put more money back into the pockets of those who rely on their cars for work, we are also permanently increasing the generosity of tax free mileage rates to support around 2 million employees and 1 million self-employed people across the UK. 

 • 
 Cheaper EV charging: At the same time, more drivers than ever are going electric – but we know the rising cost of charging vehicles risks slamming the brakes on that progress. That’s why we’re cutting prices at local, lower-powered public chargers to reduce costs for electric vehicle drivers who rely on them – saving them £150 per year on average.

 Housing 

 • 
 Helping people own a home: The Your First Home Scheme will help 70,000 people onto the property ladder and save first time buyers hundreds of pounds a month. 

 • 
 Building more affordable homes: The Prime Minister has been clear on his ambition to deliver the biggest boost to council housebuilding since the post-war period. This budget provides a further £1.5 billion in funding for social and affordable housing, taking total capital investment over the next 10 years above £40 billion. We are also exempting smaller housing developments on brownfield land from Biodiversity Net Gain requirements, making it cheaper and simpler to build. 

 • 
 Helping first-time buyers save: A new First Time Buyer ISA will provide a simpler route to saving for a deposit, while from today the Lifetime ISA withdrawal charge will be reduced to 20% so that first-time buyers purchasing a home above the existing £450,000 property price cap will not be penalised. 

 • 
 Tackling rough sleeping: We’re backing the ambition to end rough sleeping for good, with a further £432 million over the next two years to help people off the streets.

 Business 

 • 
 Delivering the government’s commitments on business rates: This year’s Budget backs England’s high streets with a package that means that all retail, hospitality and leisure properties in England will see their business rates either frozen in real terms, reduced, or cut to zero. On top of the extra 20% business rates cut for pubs and all but the largest live music venues, announced in July, this package will take around 70,000 more retail, hospitality and leisure businesses out of business rates by increasing the Small Business Rates Relief threshold. As a result, half of all retail, hospitality and leisure properties will pay no business rates. The Chancellor has also announced a two-year real-terms freeze in business rates bills for all retail, hospitality and leisure properties. 

 • 
 Fairly funded: The package will be paid for by tackling non-compliance on online marketplaces, increasing gambling tax on higher-risk machine games, and extending a 1p supplement for businesses that have seen reductions or smaller increases in their business rates bills. 

 • 
 Targeting support on thriving high streets: As part of efforts to clean up and strengthen our high streets, vape shops and adult gaming centres will also no longer benefit from certain business rates reliefs. This helps to ensure support is targeted towards the shops, pubs, cafés and other businesses that help local communities thrive. 

 • 
 As business rates are devolved in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Devolved governments will receive Barnett Consequentials which they can use to fund equivalent measures, should they choose to do so. 

 • 
 Addressing industrial energy prices: The government is delivering one of the most significant interventions in business energy costs in a generation. From April 2027, the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme will support over 10,000 eligible businesses in electricity intensive Industrial Strategy sectors and the foundational sectors in their supply chains, cutting their electricity bills by up to 25% and bringing electricity costs closer to other economies in Europe.

 Growth in every postcode 

 Economic growth is the route to higher wages, stronger public services and greater opportunity. The Budget backs Britain’s industrial strengths, helps businesses start and scale, unlocks private investment and gives places greater control over their economic future. 

 • 
 Backing British aerospace: Aerospace is one of the UK’s greatest manufacturing success stories, with a genuine competitive advantage across prime manufacturers and supply chains. A multi-decade cooperation agreement with Rolls-Royce, starting with a joint 10-year, £2.5 billion programme, will develop next-generation gas turbine technology for civil and defence aerospace, supporting 3,300 jobs in the next few years with the potential to create tens of thousands of jobs and billions in further investment across the supply chain for decades to come. This is reindustrialisation in action, backing technology, engineering skills and the UK’s security and success. 

 • 
 Life sciences investment: The government is also announcing three new public-private investments in Life Sciences, totalling over £1 billion and backed by almost £70 million in grant funding, delivering on the Modern Industrial Strategy’s commitment to reinforcing the UK’s position as a global Life Sciences superpower: Convatec will invest over £500 million over the next decade in a new global R&D hub in Manchester, Vertex Pharmaceuticals will invest over £300 million in a new facility in Oxford, and Kindeva will invest £200 million in Loughborough.

 Backing British businesses to innovate and grow 

 The government’s ambition is to make the UK the best place in the world to start a business, scale it, and stay here for the long-term. The Budget supports wealth creation by cementing the UK’s world leading tax offer for founders and their companies, with a step change in how procurement supports the UK innovation economy. 

 • 
 Backing entrepreneurs and scaling businesses: We are introducing a new Founders Relief, to encourage founders to scale their companies here in the UK, and when the time comes, reinvest in the next British success story. It will offer eligible founders of high-growth, innovative companies a reduced 10% rate of Capital Gains Tax on up to £10 million of lifetime gains. We are also tripling the trading allowance from £1,000 to £3,000 to support people starting a business; improving venture capital schemes and simplifying access to R&D tax reliefs to help growing firms attract investment and innovate; and we are expanding tax-advantaged employee share schemes to help ambitious businesses recruit and retain talent.   

 • 
 Attracting talent: We are committing to reform the visa system to deliver the most pro-business migration system in Europe for highly skilled workers, expanding the High Potential Individual visa to graduates from the world’s top 150 institutions, changing visa salary requirements to help employers across the UK hire the people they need, extending the Graduate visa to two years for eligible universities, and giving the highest-skilled workers longer to find a new job, all helping businesses attract the
